note.note:
History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
46-year-old right-handed woman with 2-week history of progressive numbness, tingling, and subjective weakness of the left arm (palmar 2nd–4th digits to elbow) plus a prior transient left-eye visual field loss; clinician suspects possible demyelinating disease and has arranged urgent neurology referral.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Progressive numbness/tingling in left arm.  
• Onset & course: Began ≈2 weeks ago after starting boxing classes; initially mild tingling, now constant numbness extending from elbow to hand with intermittent shoulder discomfort on movement; symptoms worsening.  
• Character: Palmar surface of 2nd, 3rd, 4th fingers; numbness > pain; associated subjective weakness (difficulty playing piano, occasional object-dropping).  
• Aggravating/relieving factors: None; not improved by massage, warm baths, or ibuprofen.  
• Associated symptoms: One episode a few weeks ago of transient (≈20 min) left-eye peripheral visual loss; occasional “tired” headaches and general fatigue; no seizures, no neck pain, no lower-limb symptoms.  
• Pertinent negatives: No facial droop, speech disturbance, seizures, or loss of consciousness.

Past Medical History:
• Generally healthy.  
• Recent viral-like upper respiratory illness ≈1 month ago (2 weeks duration).  
• No chronic conditions reported.

Medications:
• Ibuprofen – dose/route/frequency not documented (PRN for musculoskeletal pain).  
• Vitamin D – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Iron supplement – dose/route/frequency not documented (taken irregularly).  
• Melatonin – dose/route/frequency not documented (PRN for sleep).  
Allergies: Not documented.

Social History:
• Physically active; recently started boxing classes.  
• Right-handed; plays piano.  
• Occasional heavy alcohol use (recent binge described); smoking and recreational drugs not mentioned.  
• Occupation not stated.

Family History:
• Father: Hypothyroidism and unspecified autoimmune disorder.  
• Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, hyperlipidemia.  
• No known familial neurologic diseases.

Physical Examination:
Vitals: Not recorded.  
Exam findings: None documented during teleconsultation.

Investigations:
• Urgent neurology referral arranged for further evaluation (expected MRI brain ± spine).  
• No laboratory or imaging results available yet.

Assessment & Plan:
Overall Impression:
Progressive focal sensory deficit of left upper limb with previous transient visual disturbance – concerning for central demyelinating process (e.g., multiple sclerosis) but differential includes cervical radiculopathy and median neuropathy.

DDx Integration (consistent with transcript):
1. Multiple sclerosis – transient monocular visual loss + evolving unilateral sensory deficit; age/sex appropriate; family autoimmune tendency supports.  
2. Cervical radiculopathy (C7) – dermatomal distribution, onset after repetitive neck/upper-body activity; shoulder discomfort supports, lack of neck pain opposes.  
3. Median nerve entrapment – palmar 2nd–4th digit involvement; boxing-related wrist trauma possible; proximal arm symptoms oppose.

Issue 1: Left upper limb numbness/weakness, rule out demyelinating disease  
• Plan:  
  – Urgent neurology referral (already initiated).  
  – Anticipate MRI brain and spine, visual evoked potentials, and full neurologic examination.  
  – No disease-specific treatment until diagnosis confirmed; steroids may be considered by neurology if acute demyelination identified.  
  – Red-flag advice: attend Emergency Department if weakness spreads to legs, vision worsens, headache/vomiting/fits occur.  
  – Follow-up: Await neurology appointment; primary care review if symptoms change.

Issue 2: Right hand knuckle pain from boxing (minor musculoskeletal injury)  
• Plan:  
  – Continue ibuprofen as needed (advise not to exceed OTC dosing).  
  – Rest/modify boxing activity; consider protective taping or gloves.  
  – Re-evaluate if persistent pain or functional limitation.

Issue 3: Recent viral illness, fatigue, general health maintenance  
• Plan:  
  – Encourage adequate rest, hydration, gradual return to exercise.  
  – Continue vitamin D supplementation; discuss adherence to iron if indicated by PCP.  
  – Consider basic blood work (CBC, ferritin, thyroid panel) at primary care follow-up if fatigue persists (not ordered during current consult).

General plan items:
• Educate regarding moderation of alcohol to reduce neurologic risk factors.  
• Document and verify drug and other allergies at next opportunity.  
• Ensure patient has contact information for urgent concerns.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: Allergies, vitals, complete physical exam, occupation, smoking status not documented.  
● No direct conflicts between transcript and DDx noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear, but limited objective exam possible via teleconsultation.
